record.action: Establish ordinary dental care and a sustainable movement routine. Invite the partner to discuss health goals.
record.qualification: This is a flexible planning window. No direct trial establishes a three-year cosmetic preparation period.

record.action: If a chronic condition or future surgery is relevant, discuss how pregnancy might affect the plan.
record.qualification: Changes to prescribed drugs or elective surgery need a clinician who knows the indication.

record.action: Revisit medication, family history and vaccination records if plans change. Continue routine habits.
record.qualification: Merge with the earlier period if there is nothing new to address.

record.action: Arrange preconception care if diabetes, thyroid disease, medication exposure or reproductive history needs attention.
record.qualification: Visit timing reflects access and complexity. Individual risk determines tests.

record.action: Review medicines, supplements, acne products and vaccine timing. Check prenatal labels.
record.qualification: Some vaccines are appropriate before pregnancy. Product-specific restrictions need review.

record.action: If pregnancy is possible, begin or continue average-risk folic acid and review any higher-risk history.
record.qualification: The evidence supports starting at least a month before conception. Do not postpone folic acid until a predicted pregnancy date.

record.action: Continue folic acid and confirm the medication plan.
record.qualification: Neural tube development begins before many people know they are pregnant.

record.action: Use fertile-window information if helpful. Seek fertility evaluation according to age, duration and history.
record.qualification: ASRM suggests 12 months if under 35, 6 months from 35, potentially immediate evaluation over 40 or with known risk factors. Partner assessment may proceed in parallel.

record.action: Arrange prenatal care. Continue folic acid in early pregnancy and seek help if nausea prevents fluid intake.
record.qualification: Gestational age is counted from the last menstrual period in standard dating, roughly two weeks before fertilization in a typical cycle. No automatic supplement stacking.

record.action: Review comfortable activity, nutritional intake and any leakage or pelvic girdle pain.
record.qualification: Assessment can identify who needs pelvic floor relaxation, strengthening or other care.

record.action: Plan labor support, birth preferences, early recovery help and how to reach the care team.
record.qualification: Optional perineal massage was studied from around week 35. Breech concerns need maternity-team review.

record.action: Discuss position, analgesia, warm compresses and a chosen support person. Revisit preferences as labor changes.
record.qualification: Clinical circumstances, epidural, consent and delivery route matter. Keep assisted vaginal and cesarean care available.

record.action: Prioritize bleeding, blood pressure symptoms, pain control, feeding support and safe mobility with the maternity team.
record.qualification: Emergency symptoms need immediate care. Cesarean, major tears and complications change monitoring and the discharge plan.

record.action: Check wound symptoms, emotional wellbeing and practical support. Arrange earlier care for problems.
record.qualification: Worsening pain, spreading redness, new wound opening or fever requires prompt contact. Sudden breathlessness, chest pain or severe bleeding need emergency care.

record.action: Make contact with the postpartum clinician within three weeks; earlier or more often according to risk. Discuss sleep, feeding, contraception and comfort.
record.qualification: Ongoing care is indicated even after uncomplicated birth. No mandatory date for sex or clearance for strenuous exercise.

record.action: Complete comprehensive postpartum assessment by 12 weeks. Ask about persistent leakage, heaviness, mood, painful sex or incision symptoms.
record.qualification: Feeding choices, surgical recovery and ongoing conditions alter needs. Painful penetration is a reason to pause and seek care.

record.action: Progress activity as recovery allows. Shedding can peak near month four. Check in about pain, sleep and mood.
record.qualification: Lactation changes nutrient needs and medicine decisions. Running readiness is individual.

record.action: If separation, weakness or heaviness affects daily life, ask about pelvic-health rehabilitation.
record.qualification: One strength program was studied at 6–12 months postpartum. It provides no immediate postsurgical clearance.

record.action: Review persistent hair loss, pelvic symptoms or bothersome scars. Continue primary-care follow-up.
record.qualification: Urgent maternal warning signs remain relevant through one year. Lactation exposure still depends on current feeding.

record.action: Discuss symptoms that continue to affect function, future pregnancy plans and optional specialist review.
record.qualification: These months organize follow-up. They are not a validated recovery deadline.

record.action: Revisit reproductive plans and personally meaningful function goals. Discuss late treatment only if wanted.
record.qualification: Subsequent pregnancy, breastfeeding and surgical history affect individual options.

record.action: Persistent pain, incontinence or hernia deserves assessment at any time. Specialist care remains optional for appearance changes.
record.qualification: Long-term outcome and safety evidence is often sparse. The care pathway follows current symptoms and goals.
